title: Code-anchored lessons: sutra_remember / contextual surfacing
description:
## Problem Statement

Sutra models the codebase as it is now (structure, conventions, edges) but not what we've learned about it over time. Today that gap is filled by vidhi-reflect mining bug history into a markdown ledger, which gets injected into every session via CLAUDE.md — a broadcast with a hard budget of ~10 entries. This is the inverted-bar problem: the write bar is so high (everything costs context on every turn) that most learned knowledge never gets recorded, and what does get recorded competes for scarce always-on slots.

## Solution

Code-anchored lessons: a shared sqlite store of negative knowledge (things learned about code that a future editor needs to know), surfaced contextually through sutra tools agents already call. Lessons are the complement to conventions — conventions say "do this," lessons say "don't do that, here's why."

Agents write lessons freely during sessions. Quality is controlled through a reactive confidence lifecycle: lessons are born unverified, gain confidence through citation in yojana close-outs, and decay/archive if uncited. No human approval gate on write; the human curation is in the system design (structured close-outs, vidhi-reflect pruning), not in per-lesson approval.

The `<engineering_lessons>` CLAUDE.md block shrinks from ~10 always-injected entries to a pointer. No cardinality cap, no broadcast tax.

## User Stories

1. As an agent fixing a bug, I want to record what I learned so that future agents working in the same area see the warning without anyone remembering to tell them.
2. As an agent reading a symbol with `sutra_read`, I want to see relevant lessons inline in the response so that I don't have to know to ask for them.
3. As an agent assessing blast radius with `sutra_impact`, I want lessons about the affected symbols to appear as warnings so that I avoid known pitfalls.
4. As an agent orienting on a component with `sutra_orient`, I want to see lessons alongside conventions so that I get both the prescription and the scar tissue.
5. As an agent writing new code that imports rusqlite, I want sqlite-related lessons to surface so that I don't repeat mistakes from other projects.
6. As an agent, I want to explicitly query "what do we know about sqlite in this codebase" via `sutra_lessons` so that I can proactively check before writing new code in an unfamiliar area.
7. As an agent citing a lesson during a bug close-out, I want that citation to increase the lesson's confidence so that proven lessons surface more reliably.
8. As an agent, I want unverified lessons to only surface when no verified lessons cover the same context so that I'm not overwhelmed by low-confidence noise.
9. As an agent, I want lessons flagged as `[unverified]` when they are so that I can weigh them appropriately.
10. As an agent, I want to flag a lesson as wrong or outdated so that its confidence drops and it eventually stops surfacing.
11. As Josh, I want lessons to decay and auto-archive if they're never cited so that the store doesn't accumulate stale noise without a manual pruning obligation.
12. As Josh, I want vidhi-reflect to prune decayed lessons, flag stale ones, and merge duplicates so that lesson quality improves without manual curation.
13. As Josh, I want cross-project lessons (e.g., sqlite write discipline) to surface in any project that uses the relevant technology so that knowledge isn't siloed per project.
14. As Josh, I want lessons categorized by flat tags (rust, dart, sqlite, concurrency, etc.) so that a Dart project never sees rust-only lessons.
15. As an agent, I want to provide only text and location anchors (the symbol/file I was editing) when writing a lesson so that writing lessons is low ceremony.
16. As sutra, I want to infer pattern anchors (import patterns, directory globs) and categories from my graph when a lesson is written so that lessons are well-anchored without burdening the writer.
17. As Josh, I want existing ledger.md lessons (L1–L12) migrated to the shared store as verified lessons so that proven knowledge isn't lost in the transition.
18. As an agent running vidhi-reflect, I want to write mined lessons to the shared store instead of appending markdown to ledger.md so that lessons are durable and queryable.
19. As an agent, I want lessons to carry provenance (source task IDs, project origin, creation date) so that I can trace why a lesson exists.
20. As sutra, I want verified lessons whose anchored code has changed to surface with a `stale` flag so that they're reviewed rather than blindly trusted.

## Implementation Decisions

### Storage

- Shared sqlite DB at `~/.sutra/lessons.db`, separate from per-workspace `index.db` files. Co-located with sutra's existing DB directory.
- WAL mode for concurrent reads from multiple sutra instances. Single-writer concern is bounded (lessons written infrequently).
- Own migration system, independent of the per-workspace migration chain.
- Tables: `lessons` (core fields), `anchors` (lesson_id, kind, value — both location and pattern), `categories` (lesson_id, tag), `citations` (lesson_id, task_id, field, timestamp).
- FTS5 virtual table on `lessons.text` for explicit queries via `sutra_lessons`.

### Data model

A lesson has:
- `id` (ULID), `text`, `created_by` (agent/human), `created_at`, `project_origin`
- Location anchors (provided by writing agent): symbol name, file path
- Pattern anchors (inferred by sutra): import pattern, directory glob
- Categories: flat tags, multi-valued, partially inferred. Dimensions: technology (rust, dart, sqlite), architectural (mcp-server, daemon), concern (concurrency, sentinel-values)
- Confidence lifecycle: `verified` (bool), `confidence` (numeric), `citations` list, `last_surfaced`, `last_cited`, `archived` (bool)
- Provenance: `source_tasks` (task IDs), `project_origin`
- Staleness: `verified_at` timestamp, `content_hash_at_verification` for detecting code drift

### Modules

**LessonsDb** — the deep module. New struct with its own sqlite connection to the shared DB. Encapsulates:
- Schema and migrations
- Write path: accept text + location anchors, enrich with pattern anchors/categories using caller's workspace DB data, persist
- Read path: match lessons against a context (symbol, file, imports, component, language), apply surfacing rules
- Confidence lifecycle: citation recording, staleness via content hash
- Decay/archive: bulk operations for vidhi-reflect pruning passes
- Interface: `store()`, `query_for_context()`, `query_fts()`, `cite()`, `flag_wrong()`, `archive_decayed()`

**Anchor matching engine** — inside LessonsDb. Given a `MatchContext` (symbol name, file path, imports list, component ID, workspace language/tech stack), resolves which lessons apply. Matching mechanisms:
- Exact symbol name match for location anchors
- File glob matching (glob crate, already a dependency)
- Import pattern matching against `ImportRow.imported_path` strings
- Directory glob matching
- Category filtering by workspace language/tech
- Surfacing priority: verified lessons always shown; unverified only when no verified lessons cover the same context

**Tool response injection** — shallow glue in `sutra_read`, `sutra_impact`, `sutra_orient`. Each builds a `MatchContext` from already-resolved data and calls `LessonsDb::query_for_context()`. Results appear as a `lessons` array in the response JSON.

**Two new MCP tools:**
- `sutra_remember` — write endpoint. Accepts text + location anchors + optional source_tasks. Enriches via workspace DB, writes to shared store.
- `sutra_lessons` — explicit query. FTS5 text search + structured filters (category, symbol, verified status, project).

**Citation tracking** — explicit `sutra_remember(cite: lesson_id)` call for mid-session citation. Plus sutra can scan yojana close-out fields for lesson ID references during vidhi-reflect passes.

### SutraServer wiring

- Add `lessons_db: Arc<LessonsDb>` to `SutraServer`
- Opened once at server startup (not per-workspace)
- Passed into `tool_context()` or directly to the three tool `handle()` functions as a new argument
- `sutra_remember` and `sutra_lessons` route to `LessonsDb` methods

### Anchor enrichment

When `sutra_remember` is called, the writing sutra instance enriches the lesson before persisting:
1. Location anchors are stored as-is (agent-provided symbol name, file path)
2. Sutra looks up the file in its workspace index → gets imports via `Db::imports_for_file()`
3. Infers import-pattern anchors from the file's imports
4. Infers directory pattern from the file path
5. Infers categories from file language, import patterns, component membership, and existing convention tags

### Surfacing rules

- Verified lessons: always shown when anchors match the context
- Unverified lessons: shown only when no verified lessons cover the same context; flagged as `[unverified]`
- Category filtering: sutra knows the workspace language/tech stack, filters out irrelevant categories
- Stale verified lessons: shown with `[stale]` flag when anchored code's content hash has changed since verification
- Volume: no hard cap — the combination of anchor specificity and category filtering naturally limits what surfaces

### Confidence lifecycle

1. Birth: confidence = 0, verified = false
2. Citation in close-out: confidence rises, citation recorded with task ID and timestamp
3. Anti-verification (agent flags as wrong): confidence drops
4. Verification threshold: once cited N times (exact threshold TBD, likely 2-3), `verified` flips to true
5. Decay: unverified + uncited within time window → auto-archived by vidhi-reflect
6. Staleness: verified lessons with changed content hash → `stale` flag, still surface but flagged

### vidhi-reflect evolution

The skill's process gains:
- Tier (c) entries write to `sutra_remember` instead of `<engineering_lessons>` in manas-instructions.md
- New pruning pass: archive unverified lessons past decay window
- New staleness pass: flag verified lessons whose anchored code changed
- New dedup/merge pass: consolidate overlapping lessons
- Watermark stored in lessons.db (a `metadata` table) instead of ledger.md header
- Existing tier artifacts (rules.toml, playbooks, project CLAUDE.md) continue unchanged

### Migration path

- One-time vidhi-reflect pass: parse ledger.md L1–L12, create lessons with inferred anchors, mark as verified (they've proven themselves through the ledger's high write bar), preserve provenance (task IDs from Evidence column)
- `<engineering_lessons>` in manas-instructions.md replaced with a pointer instructing agents to use sutra_remember and cite lessons in close-outs
- ledger.md archived to `.handoffs/` for historical reference

## Testing Decisions

Tests should verify external behavior, not implementation details. Good tests for this module: given a set of stored lessons and a match context, assert the correct lessons surface with the correct flags. Don't test sqlite internals.

**LessonsDb + anchor matching engine** — the deep module, tested in isolation:
- Store/retrieve round-trips
- Anchor matching: symbol match, file glob, import pattern, directory glob
- Category filtering: language-scoped exclusion
- Surfacing priority: verified-first, unverified-as-fallback, stale flagging
- Confidence lifecycle: citation increases confidence, anti-verification decreases, verification threshold
- Decay: archived after time window without citation
- FTS5 queries: text search, structured filters
- Enrichment: given a workspace DB with import/component data, verify inferred anchors and categories

**Prior art:** `src/db/conventions.rs` tests (convention lifecycle, matching, state transitions) and constraint tests in `src/constraints/` (rule matching, violation detection, waiver filtering). Same style: set up DB state, call methods, assert results.

**Not tested:** Tool response injection (thin glue), MCP tool routing (covered by existing integration patterns), vidhi-reflect changes (prose skill, not code).

## Out of Scope

- General fact store or episode memory — lessons only
- Auto-extraction from tool failures or errors — agents write lessons deliberately
- LLM-based re-anchoring — staleness uses content hashes, not LLM judgment
- Promotion ladder or decay model from litectx — replaced by simpler citation-based confidence
- Lesson editing UI or TUI — sqlite is directly queryable
- Changes to yojana's close-out schema — citation tracking works with existing fields
- Automated cross-project lesson propagation by sutra — vidhi-reflect handles this during its passes

## Further Notes

- The lesson concept is the negative complement to conventions: conventions = "do this" (positive, auto-discovered via FCA), lessons = "don't do that, here's why" (negative, agent-curated via experience). They share surfacing channels but have different capture mechanisms.
- The ETH Zurich finding (hand-curated context +4%, LLM-generated -3%) is addressed by the reactive verification model: agent-written lessons start low-confidence and must prove themselves through citation. The quality gate is in the outcome, not the authorship.
- Cross-project scope is natural because lessons attach to technologies and patterns, not projects. The shared DB at `~/.sutra/lessons.db` is read by all sutra instances, filtered by workspace relevance.
- The naming `sutra_remember` was chosen over `sutra_lesson` (noun) to convey the action of recording experiential knowledge. `sutra_lessons` (plural) is the query endpoint.

messages.text:
Brainstorm session 2026-06-14: Reshaped from general fact/episode store to code-anchored lessons.

Research survey covered: AI coding tool memory features (Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Letta Code), MCP memory layers (AgentMemory, Memoir, Mnemo, MemNexus, Mem0, ai-memory, codebase-memory-mcp), IDE annotation tools (Swimm, CodeTour, CodeStream, Vestige, Codetations), academic literature (Sulír COMLAN 2016, Krüger FSE 2025, SATD corpus, ADR studies, tacit knowledge loss research), emerging products (Lore Protocol, Unblocked, git-why tools, Meta's context system), and convention/rule systems (AGENTS.md, Cursor Rules, Semgrep, Lattice, aicodingrules.org).

Key decisions:
- Lessons (negative knowledge), not general facts — opinionated over general
- Two anchor types: location (symbol/file) + pattern (imports/directory/tags)
- Contextual surfacing through existing tools (sutra_read/impact/orient), not a separate recall-only tool
- Human-curated, not auto-captured — ETH Zurich finding validates this
- Defer episode kind, promotion ladder, decay model from litectx
- Drop exploration_budget/confidence coupling
- Staleness detection via verified_at + content hash (from Copilot JIT validation + Lore Protocol)

The framing that crystallized: lessons are the negative complement to conventions. Conventions say 'do this.' Lessons say 'don't do that, here's why.' Same infrastructure, opposite polarity."
